newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to sign investment deal with Cuba.
newsitem.headline: France to sign investment deal with Cuba.

text.p: France will sign an investment deal with Cuba on Friday despite objections by the United States, a Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
"France will sign today an agreement with Cuba about the promotion and protection of investments with the aim of facilitating the work of companies," Rummelhardt told reporters.
"This agreement is in line with international law...We are the 19th country to sign such an agreement since 1993," he said.
The United States voiced muted criticism of the agreement on Thursday and said it hoped Paris would continue to fight for human rights on the communist-ruled island.
"We do not favour any other countries normalising their economic relations with Cuba," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said in Washington.
"But what we prefer to do...and particularly with the European Union members, is turn our joint attention on the human rights situation in Cuba," Burns told a news briefing.
The European Union and United States have been in dispute over their policies towards Cuba following the Helms-Burton law which seeks to punish some non-U.S. firms dealing with Cuba.
But the EU asked the World Trade Organisation on Monday to suspend a panel looking into the trade row after the U.S. pledged to soften the Helms-Burton law.

"We believe the presence of foreign companies could be useful for the economic and industrial development of Cuba to the benefit of its population," Rummelhardt said. He said 39 French companies were already active in Cuba.
The agreement will be signed by French Industry Minister Franck Borotra and Ibrahim Ferradaz, the Cuban minister for foreign investments and economic cooperation.
